title: Women Are Sacred 2027:
headline: A direct invitation: if you do this work, this room is for you.
story: The viewer should finish thinking “that means me.” The people who belong in that room already do the work: advocates, Tribal program staff, coalition leaders, Tribal leadership, survivors, and the young people coming up behind them.
The spine is a roll call: one role per cut, one text card each. Faces over wides. Never make it look exclusive or academic. It is for the people on the ground.
do: Open on a close face mid-laugh or mid-listen, hook text on frame 1.
Keep every role card in the same place, same size.
Pick the warmest, most human shot for each role.
Put “Survivors.” over hands or a wide, never one face.
Crop out any “Specialty Institute” sign in Durham shots.
dont: No logo, title card or fade at 0:00.
No old WAS lockup (two women holding hands), even in the background.
No images of harm or fear. No red handprint. No statistics.
No name supers. We name roles, not people.

All six role cards share one position, size and style.
